assigned.title: Playback-session candidate wire bounds match StreamCandidate bounds
assigned.acceptance: playbackSessionCandidateSchema uses THE SAME AUTHORITATIVE id and providerId limits as the StreamCandidate contract -- the exported MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_ID_CHARS and MAX_STREAM_CANDIDATE_PROVIDER_ID_CHARS -- and NOT copied numeric literals. PL-0708 exported those constants for exactly this reason; a copied literal would recreate the defect one layer out, which is the defect this task exists to close. Required: an oversized resolved candidate CANNOT RE-EXPAND ON THE SESSION WIRE after passing through another producer seam, which is the actual risk -- the contract bound governs what a provider may produce, and a second unbounded restatement downstream means the bound stops at the seam; fixture and Wikidata legitimate identifiers remain accepted, because a bound that rejects a real upstream id is an outage rather than a fix; tests cover the EXACT MAXIMUM, MAXIMUM PLUS ONE, and the serialized response, since a bound tested only from above does not prove the boundary is where it is claimed to be; reason and error output does not echo the oversized value; and NO SECOND INDEPENDENT BOUND VOCABULARY IS INTRODUCED. Note while working: playbackSessionCandidateSchema also carries unbounded uri and mimeType. They are not named in the reviewer's acceptance and are not in scope by default -- if they warrant bounds, say so and let the reviewer rule rather than adding them quietly.

review.title: apps/web declares the package it imports for the pinned transport
review.acceptance: apps/web/package.json declares @liberty/media-inspection AND package-lock.json carries the matching apps/web dependency edge, landing together in one change. PL-0308's server-bootstrap.ts imports nodePinnedFetch from @liberty/media-inspection and apps/web does not declare it; the import resolves through the root workspace symlink, so tsc and vitest are green and NO GATE CATCHES IT, which is the reason to declare it rather than a reason to leave it. Verified 2026-09-20: package-lock.json's packages['apps/web'] dependency map lists seven @liberty packages and not this one, while the manifest -- before this was reverted -- listed eight. npm ci --dry-run returned 0 in that state, so nothing is broken today; the two files simply disagree, and npm's tolerance of a link node that already exists is not a contract. WHY THIS IS A TASK AND NOT A LINE IN PL-0308: package-lock.json is reserved by PL-0710, which is in REVIEW. A task in REVIEW keeps reserving its surface so nothing mutates it mid-review, and PL-0710's approval binds to a tree hash the lockfile is part of. PL-0308 therefore reverted its own manifest line rather than ship a manifest that disagrees with a lockfile it may not touch -- the undeclared import is the pre-existing state, and a NEW inconsistency introduced into a tree under review would have been worse than the old one. Required: both files change in the SAME commit, because either alone is the disagreement this task exists to remove; the lockfile edge is produced by npm rather than hand-written; and npm ci is run from a tree with no node_modules and observed to exit 0, since a dry run against a populated tree is what made the disagreement survivable in the first place.
review.notes: Created 2026-09-20 from PL-0308. The implementer found it, declared it, and stopped when told the lockfile was not on its surface, rather than hand-editing a lockfile or leaving the two files disagreeing. Also waiting on the same release: .env.example needs the eight LIBERTY_CATALOG_* variables, held by PL-AI-0008 in REVIEW since round 47; that half is recorded in docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md with a note telling an operator the env contract does not list them yet and why. DEFINITION CORRECTION 2026-09-21, on gpt-architect's PL-0308 CHANGES_REQUESTED at e5dd889, which ordered PL-0311 BEFORE PL-0308's final approval. dependencies were ["PL-0308","PL-0710"] and PL-0308 has been removed, because that edge and the reviewer's ruling together were a DEADLOCK: PL-0308 cannot reach DONE until this task lands, and refreshReadiness holds this task in BACKLOG until every dependency is DONE, so neither could ever move. The edge was also FALSE independently of the deadlock. What this task needs from PL-0308 is that the import exists in apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts, which is committed history at ad1e1ea and readable now; a need to READ committed code is reviewDependencies, which this task already declares for that exact file, and not a lifecycle dependency. PL-0710 remains a dependency and is DONE, which is what released the package-lock.json reservation this task was waiting on.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck lint build --force, exit 0, 33 of 33 tasks (11 typecheck, 11 lint, 11 build), 0 cached. THIS GATE IS THE HONEST WEAK POINT OF THIS TASK AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN DRESSED UP: it passed identically BEFORE the change. The import resolves through the root workspace symlink whether or not apps/web declares it, so tsc, eslint, next build, vitest and npm ci --dry-run were all green against the undeclared state. That is precisely why the reviewer called it a blocker despite nothing failing -- a manifest that does not describe a dependency the code imports is a false description, not a broken build. What this gate DOES establish is that declaring it broke nothing: the same 33 tasks pass on the integrated tree.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2667 passed 1 skipped -- byte for byte the round-60 figure, because this task adds no test and changes no code path. test:scripts 0 (38 environment, 69 control-plane, 16 validate-repo assertion groups, 35 dispatcher). repo:validate 0. ai:validate 0 at 65 tasks. THE EVIDENCE THAT ACTUALLY BEARS ON THIS TASK IS THE CLEAN-TREE INSTALL THE ACCEPTANCE DEMANDED, and it was run as written rather than as a dry run: node_modules was REMOVED (ls reports No such file or directory, recorded before the install), then npm ci --no-audit --no-fund exited 0, added 483 packages in 39s. The acceptance called for exactly this because a dry run against a populated tree is what let the disagreement survive in the first place -- npm tolerates a link node that already exists, so the earlier npm ci --dry-run 0 proved nothing about a fresh clone. After the install, node_modules/@liberty/media-inspection is a symlink to ../../packages/media-inspection, and require.resolve('@liberty/media-inspection/package.json') from apps/web resolves to packages/media-inspection/package.json. THE LOCKFILE EDGE WAS PRODUCED BY NPM, NOT HAND-WRITTEN, as required: npm install --package-lock-only exited 0 and wrote exactly one line, "@liberty/media-inspection": "0.1.0" inside packages['apps/web'].dependencies, in sorted position. Both files landed in ONE commit, which the acceptance required because either alone IS the disagreement this task exists to remove. Starting state recorded for the reviewer: manifest and lockfile AGREED with each other at seven @liberty packages and both disagreed with the source, which imports an eighth in apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts and its test; git log shows apps/web/package.json was last written by PL-0305's corrective at 33195d5, never by PL-0308, which reverted its own manifest line in round 58 rather than ship a manifest disagreeing with a lockfile then reserved by PL-0710. FINDING, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE BECAUSE IT IS OFF THIS SURFACE: nothing in the repository can catch this defect class. An undeclared workspace import is invisible to every gate the project runs, so the next one will also be found by a human reader or not at all. A manifest-versus-import consistency check belongs in PL-AI-0002's CI scope; this task declares only apps/web/package.json and package-lock.json and did not widen to add one.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests
